80:   name in a config. Scripts a worker wrote are answered AFTER I read them (isolation: sandbox()/box.sh, scratch paths, no env dump).
81: - The maintainer also answers prompts and says "merge" inside worker panes; `once` presses nothing when no dialog is left. Check
82:   `gh pr list`/branches before acting on a worker's claim.
83: - Merges only on the maintainer's explicit word; then `git pull --ff-only` in main, deploy batch if `src/` changed. Check `git config --get core.worktree`
84:   in main before git operations there (it was corrupted 4 times before #10; none since).
85: - Hooks (hk 2.11.0) are safe in linked worktrees since #10: workers commit and push normally.
86: - Never print the environment. Never build in the main checkout outside the deploy script. Public text (PRs, commits, docs) never names
87:   private fleet repos, hosts or paths (run it through the redactor `--profile public` when unsure).
88: 
89: ## Step 4 launch (after compaction)
90: Goal: read-only RESEARCH workers in parallel (rog-redact, rog-roles, rog-rename (all three approved 2026-11-08); no PRs; each writes `.state/<name>/report.md`), then I write the decision document
91: (`notes/step4-decision-skeleton.md` -> D1..D8), the maintainer decides in one sitting, then a `rog-triage` worker applies the TODO/README triage.
92: Reports are read in the workers' worktrees (`[redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-*/.state/<name>/report.md`) until retired. Cost so far: workers cost $10-75 each.
93: ```
94: cd [redacted:repo]:.state/rog-orch
95: bin/launch-worker.sh --input notes/step4-inputs.md --input ~/.config/nvim/scripts/session_redact.py \
96:     rog-redact research/redaction briefs/step4-rog-redact.md
97: bin/launch-worker.sh --input journal.md --input bin/watch --input bin/lib-once.sh --input bin/stages.mjs --input bin/once \
98:     --input bin/deploy-main.sh --input notes/signal-notes.md --input notes/step4-inputs.md --input briefs/rog-memory.md \
99:     rog-roles research/roles briefs/step4-rog-roles.md
100: # rog-rename: APPROVED by the maintainer on 2026-11-08 ("yes", after D2 was restored). Launch it with the other two:
101: bin/launch-worker.sh rog-rename research/rename briefs/step4-rog-rename.md        # no inputs; read-only npm view / gh search only
102: ```
103: Each worker first replies with a PLAN and waits for my "go" (send it with `herdr agent prompt <name> "..."`). Run `bin/watch rog-redact rog-roles rog-rename` to answer prompts (it stops on anything not vetted: read it, then `bin/once`). The redaction worker builds a mock OpenAI-compatible
104: provider in its sandbox (opencode fetches the adapter into the sandbox cache: expected). Retire each with `bin/retire-worker.sh <name>` after
105: its report is read and the maintainer has what he needs from it.
106: 
107: ## Pitfalls
108: - `herdr agent prompt` right after `agent start` is lost about half the time: `launch-worker.sh` verifies and resends. The session id exists only after the first message.
109: - opencode.db is 10 GB: always filter by session_id / time. A Bun child exiting right after a large write loses the tail through a pipe.
110: - A permission dialog with empty command text: reject, ask for a script file + one-line command.
111: - zsh does not word-split unquoted variables: loops over `$F` silently read nothing and print zeros that look like a clean scan. Use arrays under `bash -c`.
112: - `launch-worker.sh --dry-run` still runs `git fetch` (a ref write); harmless, but not for plan mode.
113: - `/tmp` is cleaned after 10 days and reboots lose it: nothing durable there. Sandboxes under `.state/*/tmp/` need their own git root.
114: - A fresh worktree needs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` before its first commit (hk's prettier step).
115: - Public repo: never publish raw exports; the redactor cannot prove absence, the maintainer reads every transcript before merge.
116:

# watch NAME...: poll workers; answer "Allow once" (never "always") to a blocked worker only when the prompt is a

set -u

max=1500

**Output:**
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lib-once.sh: answer an opencode permission dialog with "Allow once" ONLY, verified on the screen.
# The highlighted option of the dialog has the yellow background 48;2;229;200;144 in the ANSI snapshot.
# Incident 2026-11-02 23:3x: a blind Enter once opened the "Always allow" confirmation, so never send Enter unverified.

_screen_ansi() { herdr agent read "$1" --source visible --lines 40 --format ansi 2>/dev/null; }

# once_highlighted NAME: succeeds when "Allow once" is the highlighted option of a visible permission dialog.
once_highlighted() { _screen_ansi "$1" | grep -aq '48;2;229;200;144mAllow once'; }

# press_once NAME: returns 0 after a verified "Allow once"; 1 when no safe state was reached (nothing confirmed);
# 2 when an "Always allow" confirmation showed up anyway (it is cancelled, see the log line).
press_once() {
  local name=$1 i
  _screen_ansi "$name" | grep -aq 'Allow once' || return 1
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    once_highlighted "$name" && break
    herdr agent send-keys "$name" left >/dev/null 2>&1
    sleep 0.6
  done
  once_highlighted "$name" || return 1
  herdr agent send-keys "$name" enter >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 1.5
  if _screen_ansi "$name" | grep -aq 'Always allow'; then
    herdr agent send-keys "$name" right >/dev/null 2>&1
    sleep 0.5
    herdr agent send-keys "$name" enter >/dev/null 2>&1
    return 2
  fi
  return 0
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# once NAME "note": verified "Allow once" for the worker's pending permission prompt; logs the decision.
# shellcheck source=lib-once.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib-once.sh"
STATE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
journal() { printf -- '- %s %s\n' "$(date '+%F %T')" "$*" >>"$STATE/journal.md"; }
name=${1:?usage: once NAME [note]}
if press_once "$name"; then
  journal "$name ALLOW-ONCE (manual) ${2:-}"
  echo "once: $name answered Allow once"
else
  rc=$?
  journal "$name NOT-ANSWERED rc=$rc ${2:-}"
  echo "once: $name NOT answered (rc=$rc: 1 = dialog/highlight not verified, 2 = Always-allow dialog appeared and was cancelled)"
  exit "$rc"
fi

// npm availability of candidate names: `npm view <name> name` (E404 = free), plain, scoped and de-punctuated forms.
// npm runs through npmenv.sh: minimal environment, empty npmrc, public registry. Nothing is published or reserved.
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs"

const here = new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname
const candidates = (process.argv[2] ?? "").split(",").filter(Boolean)

function view(name: string): Promise<{ name: string; status: "free" | "taken" | "error"; detail: string }> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(`${here}npmenv.sh`, ["view", name, "name", "--json"], { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] })
    let out = ""
    let err = ""
    child.stdout.on("data", (c) => (out += c))
    child.stderr.on("data", (c) => (err += c))
    child.on("close", () => {
      if (/E404|404 Not Found/.test(err + out)) resolve({ name, status: "free", detail: "E404" })
      else if (out.trim().startsWith('"') || out.trim().startsWith("[")) resolve({ name, status: "taken", detail: out.trim().slice(0, 80) })
      else resolve({ name, status: "error", detail: (err || out).trim().slice(0, 120) })
    })
  })
}

const forms = new Set<string>()
for (const c of candidates) {
  forms.add(c)
  forms.add(`@silopolis/${c.replace(/^opencode-/, "")}`)
  forms.add(`@silopolis/${c}`)
  forms.add(c.replaceAll("-", "")) // npm refuses names that differ only by punctuation from an existing one
  forms.add(c.replaceAll("-", "_"))
  forms.add(c.replaceAll("-", "."))
}
const list = [...forms]
const results: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof view>>[] = []
let next = 0
await Promise.all(
  Array.from({ length: 6 }, async () => {
    while (next < list.length) {
      const name = list[next++]!
      results.push(await view(name))
    }
  }),
)
const byName = new Map(results.map((r) => [r.name, r]))
const lines: string[] = []
for (const c of candidates) {
  const f = (n: string) => `${byName.get(n)?.status ?? "?"}`
  lines.push(
    `${c.padEnd(28)} plain=${f(c)} scoped-short=${f(`@silopolis/${c.replace(/^opencode-/, "")}`)} scoped-full=${f(`@silopolis/${c}`)} nohyphen=${f(c.replaceAll("-", ""))} underscore=${f(c.replaceAll("-", "_"))} dot=${f(c.replaceAll("-", "."))}`,
  )
}
const errors = results.filter((r) => r.status === "error")
lines.push("", `npm view calls: ${results.length}, errors: ${errors.length}`)
for (const e of errors) lines.push(`  ERROR ${e.name}: ${e.detail}`)
writeFileSync(process.argv[3] ?? `${here}../evidence/names-npm.txt`, lines.join("\n") + "\n")
console.log(lines.join("\n"))

```

import { decide } from "../../../src/decide.js"
import { buildBashRules, loadRules } from "../../../src/rules.js"

  .split("\n")

  .filter(Boolean)
  .map((row) => row.split("\t"))

const verdictsAfterStrip: Record<string, number> = {}

const strip = (c: string): string => {
  for (;;) {
    const a = cdRe.exec(c)
    const b = asRe.exec(c)
    if (a && !c.includes("..")) c = a[4]
    else if (b) c = b[1]
    else return c
  }
}
let raw = 0
const rawByClass: Record<string, Record<string, number>> = {}
for (const [n, info] of byLine) {
  if (info.kind !== "decision:allow-once" || info.manual) continue

  raw++
  const v = decide(text, rules).verdict
  verdicts[v] = (verdicts[v] ?? 0) + 1
  const s = decide(strip(text), rules).verdict
  verdictsAfterStrip[s] = (verdictsAfterStrip[s] ?? 0) + 1
  ;(rawByClass[info.cls] ??= {})[s] = ((rawByClass[info.cls] ??= {})[s] ?? 0) + 1
}

// shape of the decisions that needed a human note (counts of mentions, not text)
const manual = [...byLine].filter(([, i]) => i.kind === "decision:allow-once" && i.manual).map(([n]) => lines[n - 1])
const has = (re: RegExp) => manual.filter((l) => re.test(l)).length
const shape = {

  mention_isolated_env: has(/isolated|XDG|HOME/),

  mention_network_or_download: has(/curl|gh api|download|ls-remote|bun add|mise install/),
  mention_mise_run: has(/mise run/),
  mention_rm: has(/\brm\b|rmdir/),
}
const maint = {

  lines_mentioning_maintainer_approved: lines.filter((l) => /^- /.test(l) && /maintainer.{0,12}(approved|OK|said|asked|decided)|approved plan|maintainer-approved/i.test(l)).length,
}
const out = {
  raw_logged_commands: raw,
  today_shared_policy_verdict_on_raw_as_logged: verdicts,
  today_shared_policy_verdict_after_cd_and_assignment_strip: verdictsAfterStrip,
  raw_by_class_after_strip: rawByClass,
  shape,
  maint,
}
writeFileSync(".state/rog-roles/evidence/census-policy.json", `${JSON.stringify(out, null, 2)}\n`)
console.log(JSON.stringify(out, null, 2))

// Public registry metadata of the npm names that are taken (description, version, dates, downloads). No credentials.
const names = (process.argv[2] ?? "").split(",").filter(Boolean)
for (const name of names) {
  const r = await fetch(`https://registry.npmjs.org/${name.replace("/", "%2f")}`)
  if (!r.ok) {
    console.log(`${name}: HTTP ${r.status}`)
    continue
  }
  const j = (await r.json()) as {
    description?: string
    "dist-tags"?: { latest?: string }
    time?: Record<string, string>
    maintainers?: unknown[]
    repository?: { url?: string }
  }
  const d = await fetch(`https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-month/${name}`)
  const dl = d.ok ? ((await d.json()) as { downloads?: number }).downloads : `HTTP ${d.status}`
  console.log(
    `${name}: v${j["dist-tags"]?.latest} created=${j.time?.created?.slice(0, 10)} modified=${j.time?.modified?.slice(0, 10)} maintainers=${j.maintainers?.length} dl/month=${dl}\n   ${(j.description ?? "").slice(0, 200)}\n   repo=${j.repository?.url ?? "-"}`,
  )
}

  NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=https://registry.npmjs.org/ NPM_CONFIG_CACHE="$(dirname "$0")/npmcache" NPM_CONFIG_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=false \

1783 17:18:08
// npm refuses to publish a name that differs from an existing one only by punctuation (- _ .). Check every separator
// combination of each finalist with `npm view` (read-only). A variant that exists would block the publish.
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs"

const here = new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname
const finalists = (process.argv[2] ?? "").split(",").filter(Boolean)

const exists = (name: string): Promise<boolean | "error"> =>
  new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(`${here}npmenv.sh`, ["view", name, "name", "--json"], { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] })
    let all = ""
    child.stdout.on("data", (c) => (all += c))
    child.stderr.on("data", (c) => (all += c))
    child.on("close", () => (/E404|404 Not Found/.test(all) ? resolve(false) : all.trim().startsWith('"') ? resolve(true) : resolve("error")))
  })

function variants(name: string): string[] {
  const parts = name.split("-")
  let out = [parts[0]!]
  for (const part of parts.slice(1)) out = out.flatMap((o) => ["-", "_", ".", ""].map((s) => o + s + part))
  return out
}

const lines: string[] = []
for (const f of finalists) {
  const vs = variants(f)
  const hits: string[] = []
  let errors = 0
  let next = 0
  await Promise.all(
    Array.from({ length: 6 }, async () => {
      while (next < vs.length) {
        const v = vs[next++]!
        const e = await exists(v)
        if (e === true) hits.push(v)
        else if (e === "error") errors++
      }
    }),
  )
  lines.push(`${f.padEnd(28)} variants checked=${vs.length} existing=${hits.length ? hits.join(",") : "none"} errors=${errors}`)
}
writeFileSync(process.argv[3] ?? `${here}../evidence/names-similar.txt`, lines.join("\n") + "\n")
console.log(lines.join("\n"))

```

3143 17:19:36 rename.ts
// Mechanical rename of the project's name families, applied to a COPY of the tracked files (never to the worktree).
//
//   bun rename.ts --to opencode-agent-policy [--command policy-review] --from-dir <git checkout> --into <empty dir>
//
// What it does: `git archive HEAD` of --from-dir into --into (tracked files only), then rewrites the name families
// in every text file except memory/ (session transcripts are history and stay as they are). The order matters: the
// longest family first, so that `opencode-readonly-guard` is not half-rewritten by the `readonly-guard` rule.
//
// It does NOT decide anything: the new name, the command name and the migration shims (old env vars, old store
// path) are the maintainer's, see the report.
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process"
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { parseArgs } from "node:util"

const { values } = parseArgs({
  options: {
    to: { type: "string" }, // full package name: opencode-<short>
    command: { type: "string" }, // review command, default <short>-review
    "from-dir": { type: "string" },
    into: { type: "string" },
  },
})
const pkg = values.to
if (!pkg || !values["from-dir"] || !values.into) throw new Error("usage: --to <pkg> --from-dir <checkout> --into <dir>")
const short = pkg.replace(/^opencode-/, "")
const command = values.command ?? `${short}-review`
const snake = short.replaceAll("-", "_")
const upper = snake.toUpperCase()

// [pattern, replacement], in this order
const families: [RegExp, string][] = [
  [/opencode-readonly-guard/g, pkg], // package, bin, plugin id, repo URL, schema $id, CLI name
  [/READONLY_GUARD/g, upper], // env vars
  [/readonly_guard/g, snake], // tool ids and the confirmation permission
  [/guard-review/g, command], // the review command
  [/readonly-guard/g, short], // store file, log dir, herdr file, error prefixes, prose
]

mkdirSync(values.into, { recursive: true })
const tar = execFileSync("git", ["archive", "HEAD"], { cwd: values["from-dir"], maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 })
execFileSync("tar", ["-x", "-C", values.into], { input: tar })

const binary = /\.(png|jpg|ico|gz|zip|lock)$/
function walk(dir: string, rel = ""): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir).flatMap((name) => {
    const path = join(dir, name)
    const r = rel ? `${rel}/${name}` : name
    return statSync(path).isDirectory() ? walk(path, r) : [r]
  })
}

let changed = 0
for (const rel of walk(values.into)) {
  if (rel.startsWith("memory/") || binary.test(rel)) continue
  const path = join(values.into, rel)
  const before = readFileSync(path, "utf8")
  let after = before
  for (const [re, to] of families) after = after.replace(re, to)
  if (after !== before) {
    writeFileSync(path, after)
    changed++
  }
}
// bun.lock is text: its workspace name is the package name
const lock = join(values.into, "bun.lock")
writeFileSync(lock, readFileSync(lock, "utf8").replaceAll("opencode-readonly-guard", pkg))
console.log(`renamed to ${pkg} (short ${short}, command ${command}, env ${upper}_*): ${changed} files rewritten`)

```

46: export interface ToolCall {

48:   args: Record<string, unknown>
49: }
50: export interface Step {

52:   tools?: ToolCall[]
53: }
54: export interface Context {

57:   marker: string

59:   step: number

65:   role: string
66:   content?: string | { type: string; text?: string }[] | null
67:   tool_calls?: unknown[]
68:   tool_call_id?: string
69: }
70: export type Script = (ctx: Context) => Step | undefined
71: 
72: export interface ScriptFile {
73:   scenarios?: Record<string, Step[]>
74:   fallback?: Step
75:   rules?: { lastUser: string; step: Step }[]
76: }
77: 
78: export interface Mock {
79:   url: string
80:   port: number
81:   stop(): void
82:   requests(): { seq: number; path: string; hasTools: boolean; body: { messages: ChatMessage[]; tools?: unknown[] } }[]
83: }
84: 
85: export const textOf = (content: ChatMessage["content"]): string =>
86:   typeof content === "string"
87:     ? content
88:     : Array.isArray(content)
89:       ? content.map((part) => (typeof part.text === "string" ? part.text : "")).join("\n")
90:       : ""
91: 
92: /** The script file format as a script function and a fallback for requests without tools. */
93: export function fromJson(file: ScriptFile): { script: Script; fallback: Script } {
94:   const scenarios = file.scenarios ?? {}
95:   return {
96:     script: (ctx) => {
97:       for (const [marker, steps] of Object.entries(scenarios)) {
98:         if (ctx.marker.includes(marker)) return steps[ctx.step] ?? { text: `done ${marker}` }
99:       }
100:       return file.fallback
101:     },
102:     fallback: (ctx) => {
103:       for (const rule of file.rules ?? []) if (new RegExp(rule.lastUser).test(ctx.lastUser)) return rule.step
104:       return file.fallback ?? { text: "Title" }
105:     },
106:   }
107: }
108: 
109: /** `scripts`: marker substring -> steps. A step past the end of the list ends with a short text. */
110: export function scenarios(scripts: Record<string, Step[]>): Script {
111:   return fromJson({ scenarios: scripts }).script
112: }
113: 
114: export function startMock(file: string, script: Script, fallback: Script = () => ({ text: "Title" })): Mock {
115:   writeFileSync(file, "")
116:   let seq = 0
117:   const log: ReturnType<Mock["requests"]> = []
118:   const server = Bun.serve({
119:     hostname: "127.0.0.1",
120:     port: 0,
121:     async fetch(request) {
122:       const path = new URL(request.url).pathname
123:       if (!path.endsWith("/chat/completions")) return new Response("not found", { status: 404 })
124:       const body = (await request.json()) as { messages: ChatMessage[]; tools?: unknown[]; model?: string }
125:       const n = ++seq
126:       const hasTools = Array.isArray(body.tools) && body.tools.length > 0
127:       const entry = { seq: n, path, hasTools, body }
128:       log.push(entry)
129:       appendFileSync(file, `${JSON.stringify(entry)}\n`)
130:       const users = body.messages.filter((message) => message.role === "user")
131:       const ctx: Context = {
132:         seq: n,
133:         marker: textOf(users[0]?.content),
134:         step: body.messages.filter((message) => message.role === "assistant").length,
135:         hasTools,
136:         lastUser: textOf(users.at(-1)?.content),
137:         messages: body.messages,
138:       }
139:       // a request without tools is the title generator or a compaction: never a scripted tool call
140:       const step = (hasTools ? script(ctx) : undefined) ?? fallback(ctx) ?? { text: "ok" }
141:       return sse(step, n, body.model ?? "scripted")
142:     },
143:   })
144:   return {
145:     url: `http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}/v1`,
146:     port: server.port!,
147:     stop: () => void server.stop(true),
148:     requests: () => log,
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: function sse(step: Step, seq: number, model: string): Response {
153:   const id = `chatcmpl-mock-${seq}`
154:   const chunk = (delta: unknown, finish: string | null = null) =>
155:     `data: ${JSON.stringify({ id, object: "chat.completion.chunk", created: 0, model, choices: [{ index: 0, delta, finish_reason: finish }] })}\n\n`
156:   let out = chunk({ role: "assistant", content: "" })
157:   if (step.text) out += chunk({ content: step.text })
158:   if (step.tools?.length) {
159:     step.tools.forEach((call, index) => {
160:       out += chunk({
161:         tool_calls: [
162:           {
163:             index,
164:             id: `call_${seq}_${index}`,
165:             type: "function",
166:             function: { name: call.name, arguments: JSON.stringify(call.args) },
167:           },
168:         ],
169:       })
170:     })
171:     out += chunk({}, "tool_calls")
172:   } else {
173:     out += chunk({}, "stop")
174:   }
175:   out += `data: ${JSON.stringify({ id, object: "chat.completion.chunk", created: 0, model, choices: [], usage: { prompt_tokens: 10, completion_tokens: 5, total_tokens: 15 } })}\n\n`
176:   out += "data: [DONE]\n\n"
177:   return new Response(out, { headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream", "cache-control": "no-cache" } })
178: }
179: 
180: if (import.meta.main) {
181:   const arg = (name: string, fallback?: string): string | undefined => {
182:     const index = process.argv.indexOf(name)
183:     return index > 0 ? process.argv[index + 1] : fallback
184:   }
185:   const scriptPath = arg("--script")
186:   if (!scriptPath) {
187:     process.stderr.write("usage: bun mock-provider.ts --script script.json --requests requests.jsonl [--port-file port.txt]\n")
188:     process.exit(64)
189:   }
190:   const { script, fallback } = fromJson(JSON.parse(readFileSync(scriptPath, "utf8")) as ScriptFile)
191:   const mock = startMock(arg("--requests", "requests.jsonl")!, script, fallback)
192:   writeFileSync(arg("--port-file", "port.txt")!, `${mock.url}\n`)
193:   process.stdout.write(`${mock.url}\n`)
194:   process.on("SIGTERM", () => {

**Tool: bash**

**Input:**
```json
{
  "command": "cd [redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-rename/.state/rog-rename/tmp && ls -la --time-style=+%T cross-repo.ts | awk '{print $5, $6}'; rtk read cross-repo.ts"

**Output:**
```
3529 17:27:22
// Cross-repo references, COUNT ONLY. Per-repo counts go to evidence/cross-repo.txt (private); the console gets
// aggregates by category. No file content is read into the output, only file paths and counts.
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process"
import { existsSync, readdirSync, realpathSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { homedir } from "node:os"
import { basename, join } from "node:path"

const home = homedir()
const work = join(home, "Work")
const SKIP = new Set(["trees", "opencode-readonly-guard"])
const PATTERN = "opencode-readonly-guard|readonly-guard|readonly_guard|READONLY_GUARD|guard-review"

type Root = { label: string; dir: string; kind: "sibling" | "dotfiles" | "skills" }
const roots: Root[] = []
for (const name of readdirSync(work)) {
  if (SKIP.has(name)) continue
  const dir = join(work, name)
  let real = dir
  try {
    real = realpathSync(dir)
  } catch {
    continue
  }
  if (/[redacted:private]/.test(real)) continue
  roots.push({ label: name, dir, kind: "sibling" })
}
const chezmoi = join(home, ".local/share/chezmoi")
if (existsSync(chezmoi) && !/[redacted:private]/.test(realpathSync(chezmoi))) roots.push({ label: "chezmoi-source", dir: chezmoi, kind: "dotfiles" })
const skills = join(home, ".agents/skills")
if (existsSync(skills)) roots.push({ label: "agents-skills", dir: skills, kind: "skills" })

function category(path: string): string {
  const base = basename(path)
  if (/\/(\.state|\.tmp)\//.test(path)) return "agent state/scratch (ignored by git)"
  if (/\/memory\/sessions\//.test(path) || /transcript|session/i.test(path)) return "session transcripts/history"
  if (/^opencode\.jsonc?$/.test(base) || /\/opencode\/.*\.jsonc?(\.tmpl)?$/.test(path)) return "opencode config"
  if (/SKILL\.md$|AGENTS\.md$|CLAUDE\.md$/.test(base) || /\/(skills|\.agents|\.claude|\.opencode)\//.test(path)) return "skills / agent instructions"
  if (/\.(md|txt|adoc)$/.test(base)) return "docs"
  if (/dot_config|private_dot|\.tmpl$/.test(path)) return "chezmoi config template"
  if (/\.(sh|bash|zsh|fish|ts|js|mjs|py|toml|ya?ml|json|pkl|nix)$/.test(base)) return "scripts / code / config"
  return "other"
}

const perRepo: string[] = []
const agg = new Map<string, number>()
let reposWith = 0
let filesTotal = 0
for (const r of roots) {
  const rg = spawnSync(
    "rg",
    ["-l", "-i", "--hidden", "--no-ignore", "--max-filesize", "2M", "-g", "!.git/", "-g", "!node_modules/", "-g", "!dist/", "-g", "!**/[redacted:private]/**", "-e", PATTERN, r.dir],
    { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 },
  )
  const files = (rg.stdout ?? "").split("\n").filter(Boolean)
  perRepo.push(`${r.kind} ${r.label}: ${files.length} files`)
  const kinds = new Map<string, number>()
  for (const f of files) {
    const c = category(f)
    kinds.set(c, (kinds.get(c) ?? 0) + 1)
    const key = `${r.kind} | ${c}`
    agg.set(key, (agg.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)
  }
  if (files.length) {
    reposWith++
    filesTotal += files.length
    for (const [c, n] of kinds) perRepo.push(`    ${c}: ${n}`)
  }
}
writeFileSync(new URL("../evidence/cross-repo.txt", import.meta.url), perRepo.join("\n") + "\n")
console.log(`roots searched: ${roots.length} (siblings ${roots.filter((r) => r.kind === "sibling").length}, dotfiles ${roots.filter((r) => r.kind === "dotfiles").length}, skills ${roots.filter((r) => r.kind === "skills").length})`)
console.log(`roots with at least one match: ${reposWith}, matching files total: ${filesTotal}`)
for (const [k, n] of [...agg].sort()) console.log(`  ${k}: ${n}`)

```

// R2 / H2: experimental.chat.messages.transform.
//   effect: turn 1 with the hook off (a secret enters the history), then the hook is switched to "redact" and
//           turn 2 is sent in the same session. What does the provider get, what do DB and API hold, how often is
//           the hook called, what does it see?
//   cost <off|values|full>: 200 assistant steps, ~1 MB of tool output in the history; wall time and in-hook time.
import { apiToolHits, requestToolHits } from "./analysis.ts"
import { assertNoLeaks, keepEvidence, lab } from "./lib.ts"

const mode = process.argv[2] ?? "effect"

if (mode === "effect") {
  const l = await lab({
    name: "transform-effect",
    setup: () => ({
      plugin: { events: false, shapes: false },
      script: {
        scenarios: {
          "SCENARIO:hist": [
            { tools: [{ name: "bash", args: { command: "printenv [redacted:envvar]", description: "print" } }] },
            { text: "first answer" },
            { text: "second answer" },
            { text: "third answer" },
          ],
        },
      },
    }),
  })
  try {
    const out = await l.serve(async (api) => {
      const sid = await api.session()
      await api.say(sid, "SCENARIO:hist")
      const afterTurn1 = { where: l.where(), requests: l.mock.requests().length }
      l.control({ hooks: { transform: "redact" } })
      await api.say(sid, "second turn")
      const messages = await api.messages(sid)
      return { sid, afterTurn1, apiHits: apiToolHits(l, messages), apiJsonHits: l.count(JSON.stringify(messages)) }
    })
    const trace = l.trace()
    const calls = trace.filter((t) => t.hook === "experimental.chat.messages.transform")
    const summary = {
      afterTurn1: out.afterTurn1,
      finalWhere: l.where(),
      apiJsonHits: out.apiJsonHits,
      requests: requestToolHits(l).perRequest,
      requestRoles: l.mock.requests().map((r) => ({ seq: r.seq, hasTools: r.hasTools, n: r.body.messages.length })),
      transformCalls: calls.map((c) => ({
        messages: c.messages,
        roles: c.roles,
        partsHit: c.partsHit,
        changed: c.changed,
        ms: c.ms,
        inputKeys: c.inputKeys,
      })),
    }
    console.log(JSON.stringify(summary, null, 1))
    keepEvidence(l, "03-transform-effect", summary)
  } finally {
    assertNoLeaks(l)
  }
} else {
  // cost
  const variant = process.argv[3] ?? "off" // off | values | full
  const STEPS = 200
  const l = await lab({
    name: `transform-cost-${variant}`,
    setup: ({ fakes }) => ({
      plugin: {
        hooks: variant === "off" ? { transform: "observe" } : { transform: "redact" },
        shapes: variant === "full",
        context: variant === "full",
        events: false,
      },
      script: {
        scenarios: {
          "SCENARIO:big": [
            ...Array.from({ length: STEPS }, (_, i) => ({
              tools: [
                {
                  name: "bash",
                  args: {
                    command:
                      i % 20 === 5
                        ? "printenv [redacted:envvar]; yes 'ordinary output line 0123456789 abcdefghij' | head -c 5000"
                        : `yes 'ordinary output line ${i} 0123456789 abcdefghij' | head -c 5000`,
                    description: `step ${i}`,
                  },
                },
              ],
            })),
            { text: "done" },
          ],
        },
      },
    }),
  })
  try {
    const t0 = performance.now()
    await l.serve(async (api) => {
      const sid = await api.session()
      await api.say(sid, "SCENARIO:big")
      return sid
    })
    const wall = performance.now() - t0
    const calls = l.trace().filter((t) => t.hook === "experimental.chat.messages.transform")
    const ms = calls.map((c) => c.ms as number)
    const requests = l.mock.requests()
    const bytes = requests.map((r) => JSON.stringify(r.body).length)
    const sum = ms.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)
    const sorted = [...ms].sort((a, b) => a - b)
    const summary = {
      variant,
      steps: STEPS,
      wallSeconds: Math.round(wall) / 1000,
      transformCalls: calls.length,
      requests: requests.length,
      hookMsTotal: Math.round(sum),
      hookMsMedian: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)],
      hookMsMax: sorted.at(-1),
      lastCallMessages: calls.at(-1)?.messages,
      lastRequestBytes: bytes.at(-1),
      requestsWithSecret: requests.filter((r) => l.count(JSON.stringify(r.body)) > 0).length,
      dbPartHits: l.where().db_part,
    }
    console.log(JSON.stringify(summary, null, 1))
    keepEvidence(l, `03-transform-cost-${variant}`, summary)
  } finally {
    assertNoLeaks(l)
  }
}

4032 17:34:04
// exp-verbs.ts: which write verbs does opencode's built-in external_directory check cover? One marker file per command.
// Harness: rog-redact's lib.ts + mock-provider.ts. Usage: bun .state/rog-roles/prototype/exp-verbs.ts
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { evidenceDir, lab } from "./lib.ts"

type Check = { name: string; command: string; effect: (O: string) => boolean }
const verbs = (O: string, P: string): Check[] => [
  { name: "mv", command: `mv m1.txt ${O}/v_mv`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_mv")) },
  { name: "mkdir", command: `mkdir ${O}/v_mkdir`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_mkdir")) },
  { name: "chmod", command: `chmod 600 ${O}/o_mode.txt`, effect: (o) => (statSync(join(o, "o_mode.txt")).mode & 0o777) === 0o600 },
  { name: "ln -s", command: `ln -s /etc/hostname ${O}/v_ln`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_ln")) },
  { name: "truncate", command: `truncate -s 5 ${O}/o_trunc.txt`, effect: (o) => statSync(join(o, "o_trunc.txt")).size === 5 },
  { name: "install", command: `install -D README.md ${O}/v_install`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_install")) },
  { name: "dd of=", command: `dd if=README.md of=${O}/v_dd status=none`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_dd")) },
  { name: "curl -o", command: `curl -s -o ${O}/v_curl file:///etc/hostname`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_curl")) },
  { name: "tar -cf", command: `tar -cf ${O}/v_tar.tar README.md`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_tar.tar")) },
  { name: "git init DIR", command: `git init -q ${O}/v_git`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_git", ".git")) },
  { name: "cd OUT && touch", command: `cd ${O} && touch v_cd`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_cd")) },
  { name: "quoted path", command: `touch "${O}/v_quoted"`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_quoted")) },
  { name: "variable path", command: `D=${O}; touch $D/v_var`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_var")) },
  { name: "command substitution", command: `touch "$(echo ${O}/v_subst)"`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_subst")) },
  { name: "eval", command: `eval "touch ${O}/v_eval"`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_eval")) },
  { name: "find -exec touch", command: `find README.md -exec touch ${O}/v_find \\;`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_find")) },
  { name: "xargs touch", command: `echo ${O}/v_xargs | xargs touch`, effect: (o) => existsSync(join(o, "v_xargs")) },
]
let checks: Check[] = []
const l = await lab({
  name: "verbs",
  project: { "README.md": "readme\n", "m1.txt": "m\n" },
  setup: ({ dir, project }) => {
    const O = join(dir, "outside")
    mkdirSync(O, { recursive: true })
    for (const f of ["o_mode.txt", "o_trunc.txt"]) writeFileSync(join(O, f), "0123456789")
    checks = verbs(O, project)
    const steps = checks.map((c) => ({ tools: [{ name: "bash", args: { command: c.command, description: "probe" } }] }))
    return {
      script: { scenarios: { "SCENARIO:verbs": [...steps, { text: "done" }] }, fallback: { text: "Title" } },
      config: { permission: { bash: "allow", read: "allow", edit: "allow", external_directory: { "*": "deny" } }, plugin: [] },
    }
  },
})
const O = join(l.box.dir, "outside")
const status = await l.serve(async (api) => {
  const id = await api.session()
  await api.say(id, "SCENARIO:verbs go")
  const messages = (await api.messages(id)) as { parts: { type: string; state?: { status: string; input?: { command?: string } } }[] }[]
  return new Map(messages.flatMap((m) => m.parts).filter((p) => p.type === "tool").map((p) => [p.state?.input?.command, p.state?.status]))
})
const rows = checks.map((c) => ({ verb: c.name, tool_status: status.get(c.command), wrote_outside: c.effect(O) }))
writeFileSync(join(evidenceDir, "verbs-external-directory.json"), `${JSON.stringify(rows, null, 1)}\n`)
console.log(rows.map((r) => `${String(r.verb).padEnd(22)} ${String(r.tool_status).padEnd(10)} wrote_outside=${r.wrote_outside}`).join("\n"))
console.log("leaks", l.finish())

```

25: ## 2. Findings
26: 
27: ### a. Role model
28: 
29: Trust assumptions: every role is trusted but fallible. This is an accident preventer, not a sandbox: a worker may edit
30: `mise.toml` and run `mise run check`, and any interpreter runs arbitrary code, so scope is enforced by parsing, not
31: containment. Symlinks are not followed. A role is defined by capabilities from a reviewed catalogue, never by free
32: patterns.
33: 
34: | Capability               | read-only          | worker                          | orchestrator                      | deployer                | reviewer          |
35: | ------------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------- |
36: | read files               | yes (no credentials) | yes                           | yes                               | yes                     | yes               |
37: | write in own worktree    | no                 | yes                             | no                                | no                      | no                |
38: | write elsewhere          | no                 | no                              | own state dir only                | only through its script | no                |
39: | scratch                  | none               | `.state/<agent>/tmp`            | `.state/<orch>/`                  | the script's clone      | none              |
40: | local git                | read               | add/commit/rebase/switch/fetch  | read, `pull --ff-only` in main    | via script              | read              |
41: | push own branch          | no                 | yes: exact name, never force    | no                                | no                      | no                |
42: | merge                    | no                 | block                           | ask (maintainer decides)          | no                      | block             |
43: | `gh` read                | ask today (gap)    | yes                             | yes                               | no                      | yes               |
44: | `gh` write               | no                 | `pr create/edit/comment`        | ask (`pr edit`, `pr merge`)       | no                      | `pr comment`      |
45: | herdr read               | yes                | yes                             | yes                               | no                      | yes               |
46: | herdr control            | no                 | block                           | own fleet `agent prompt`; rest ask or pinned script | no     | no                |
47: | network read             | ask                | yes                             | ask                               | no                      | ask               |
48: | install tools            | no                 | frozen lockfile only, rest ask  | no                                | no                      | no                |
49: | run project scripts      | no                 | `mise run` catalogue, own tree  | no                                | one pinned script       | ask               |
50: | list processes           | yes (no env forms) | yes                             | yes                               | yes                     | yes               |
51: | read the environment     | no                 | no                              | no                                | no                      | no                |
52: | read credential files    | no                 | no                              | no                                | no                      | no                |
53: 
54: A "researcher" (this worker) is the worker without git push and with writes limited to `.state/<agent>/`; the journal
55: shows it is the commonest shape (see classes C1, C2, C5 below). A reviewer appears in the data only as a hunk tab for
56: the maintainer; I kept it because `gh pr diff/comment` without any code writes is a distinct, cheap role.
57: 
58: ### b. Decision classes (`evidence/census-summary.json`, `census-policy.json`, `census-lines.tsv`; no journal text)
59: 
60: Journal: 264 event lines (my count), of which 219 are permission decisions: 199 "Allow once" (163 with a note, 36
61: logged as the raw command by the helper), 17 not answered, 3 rejected; the other 45 are deploys, launches, incidents,
62: decisions and notes. Classes were assigned by regex and 18 hand overrides (spot-checked).
63: 
64: | Class                                        | n  | Machine could decide?                                              |
65: | -------------------------------------------- | -- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
66: | C1 read-only (incl. reads of scratch files)  | 79 | yes, already by the shared allowlist; manual ones were `cd X &&`, `VAR=` prefixes, pipelines |
67: | C2 scratch write                             | 39 | yes with path scope; interpreter-written files only via pins       |
68: | C3 own-worktree dev loop (check, build, test, format, add, commit, rebase) | 49 | yes: catalogue plus cwd in worktree; never in the main checkout |
69: | C4 own-branch push, `gh pr create/edit`      | 7  | yes for the exact own branch; the PR body check (private data) stays a human or redactor step |
70: | C5 reviewed script (deploy 3, scratch 20)    | 23 | yes after one human review per content hash                        |
71: | C6 exception the maintainer approved         | 2  | no (a tool install and a package fetch outside the pinned set)     |
72: | C7 rejected                                  | 3  | one is moot in a hook (unreadable text), one is coordination (duplicate work), one needs a human (an unpublished package name in a config) |
73: | C8 helper could not press the key            | 17 | disappears: UI automation, not policy                              |
74: 
75: Shape of the 163 notes: 73 mention a scratch root, 42 own worktree or branch, 49 a reviewed script, 22 an interpreter
76: (python, perl, bun, node, awk: not scopable), 12 a network fetch or install, 10 `rm`, 8 `mise run`, 7 `gh pr`, 5 push.
77: 19 lines mention the maintainer, 13 of them record an approval. 7 lines involve `HK=0` (skips the hooks the briefs say
78: never to bypass): a recurring human variance. The 36 raw commands under today's shared rules: 19 allow, 16 ask (11
79: dev-loop commands, 5 pipeline pieces such as `sed -n 'N,Mp'`, `awk NR`, `rtk head`), 1 block (a `git add && git commit`,
80: correctly a write). Confidence: medium on class borders, high on totals.
81: 
82: ### c. Expressibility
83: 
84: What the code knows today (read from `src/`): `analyze.ts` sees redirection targets and a verb's own options, but has no
85: cwd, no scope and does not track `cd` (`parseShell` flattens a line into ordered simple commands). Facts from real
86: opencode 1.19.3 (`evidence/hooks-main.json`, `hooks-worktree.json`, `verbs-external-directory.json`: two runs of 20
87: scripted calls and one of 17, through the mock):
88: 
89: - `tool.execute.before` input is only `{tool, sessionID, callID}`; for bash the args are `command`, `description`,
90:   `workdir` (the hook sees `workdir`). `shell.env` input is `{cwd, sessionID, callID}` and `cwd` is the session
91:   directory. `chat.params` preceded every `tool.execute.before` of its session (0 exceptions in 20 calls).
92: - In a linked git worktree opened as the project, `directory = worktree = project.worktree = the linked worktree`
93:   (not the main checkout). So the built-in scope is the worker's own tree, and `touch <main>/x` is refused as external.
94:   I had guessed the opposite; the experiment contradicts it.
95: - Built-in `external_directory` (rule `{"*":"deny"}`, an allowed dir with a glob) refuses `cat`, `touch`, `rm`, `cp`,
96:   `mv`, `mkdir`, `chmod`, `cd` with literal operands (also relative `../x`, `workdir`, quoted paths), and the `write`
97:   tool. It does NOT cover: `>` redirection, `tee`, `sed -i`, `ln`, `truncate`, `install`, `dd of=`, `curl -o`, `tar`,
98:   `git init DIR`, `find -exec`, `xargs`, `eval`, `bash -c`, python, variables (`D=/x; touch $D/f`), `$(...)`; `ls`
99:   outside completes. Each uncovered one wrote a file outside.
100: - False positive, reproduced (and reported by the coordinator): `cd .state/x/tmp && true; cd ../../.. && touch f`
101:   stays inside the worktree but is refused; relative `cd` targets are resolved against the start directory.
102: - `edit` globs are relative to the project root: `{"*":"deny","src/**":"allow"}` allowed `src/new.ts`, refused
103:   `README2.md`. Writes by the `edit`/`write` tools are scopable by opencode itself; bash writes are not.
104: 
105: | Class                         | (i) 1.x `permission` globs                          | (ii) 1.x plugin hooks (block only)                               | (iii) only the 2.x hook                          |
106: | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
107: | read-only commands (C1)       | shared allowlist, exact                             | write guard                                                      | prefixes `cd X &&`, `VAR=v cmd`, any redirection |
108: | scratch/worktree writes       | `rm *`, `touch *` allows are cwd-blind              | scope check on targets and redirections, cwd tracked, `workdir`  | allow in code, no glob hole                      |
109: | dev loop (C3)                 | exact verb globs (`mise run check *`)               | cwd must be the worktree (block in main)                         | same, with the allow decided in code             |
110: | own-branch push (C4)          | exact rule generated per worker (`git push origin feat/x`); `HEAD` cannot | block other branch, refspec, force, delete        | same                                             |
111: | reviewed script (C5)          | text of one spelling per rule (abs, relative)       | resolve path after `cd`, sha256 pin, argument list: block if changed | allow only when the hash matches            |
112: | env, credentials              | deny globs miss `echo $TOKEN`, `cat file`           | block variables and credential paths                             | same                                             |
113: | human exceptions (C6, C7)     | ask                                                 | -                                                                | -                                                |
114: 
115: What globs cannot express: cwd-relative scope (`cd` is skipped by opencode's patterns); "push only my own branch"
116: without a rule generated per worker; "this script and no other" (text only, content unseen); env prefixes
117: (`HK=0 git commit`); `git -C DIR`; redirections after the first pipeline stage; and the decisive one: a hook can only
118: block, so "allow, unless the code cannot verify" is not expressible. Measured on `cases-roles.json`
119: (`prototype/run-cases.ts`, `evidence/cases-run.json`), design intent as expectation:
120: 
121: | Decider                                             | agrees (of 116) | unsafe allows |
122: | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------- |
123: | generated globs alone                               | 65              | 27            |
124: | globs + code that only blocks (1.x, honest)         | 112             | 4             |
125: | same, code turns ask into block where a glob allows | 112             | 0             |
126: | code decides (2.x semantics)                        | 116             | 0             |
127: 
128: The 4 unsafe allows are all "this script and no other": the same relative path in another directory, an unreviewed
129: argument. The 4 disagreements of the strict variant are those asks becoming blocks. Caveat: the prototype was tuned
130: against the corpus (first run 111/113; I fixed 3 prototype bugs and added 4 cases after it), so 116/116 is a fit, not a
131: validation. Confidence: high on the hook facts, medium on the numbers.
132: 
133: ### d. Config surface
134: 
135: Invariant kept in all three: a role names catalogue items (data reviewed in the repository, `rules/roles.json`) and never
136: brings patterns; any user pattern in a role still goes through `classifyPattern`; a read-only agent's write guard is
137: never switched off by a role. Evidence for how much that bites: `bun src/cli.ts vet` accepts 1 of 15 patterns a worker's
138: dev loop needs (`mise run build` exact); it refuses `git commit *`, `git add *`, `git push …`, `rm *`, `bun test *`,
139: `gh pr create *`, `herdr agent prompt …`.
140: 
141: - Option A, role per agent name (extends `agents`; recommended):
142:   `{"roles": {"plan": "read-only", "worker": {"role": "worker", "scripts": [{"path": ".state/w/tmp/x.sh", "sha256": "…"}]}, "orch": {"role": "orchestrator", "fleet": "task-"}}}`.
143:   `agents.include/exclude` stay as sugar for `read-only` / nothing. Fits `chat.params` agent tracking and the existing
144:   config hook. Needs the launcher to start the agent by name.
145: - Option B, role per session through a marker the launcher writes (`.opencode/readonly-guard.local.json`, untracked, or an
146:   env var): `{"role": "worker", "branch": "feat/x"}`. Matches `launch-worker.sh`; the maintainer's attended `build`
147:   sessions stay free. Costs: marker magic, and whether a herdr pane passes env is unverified.
148: - Option C, roles as presets: `{"presets": {"role-worker": true}}`. Smallest code, but presets are global patterns today,
149:   not per agent, and cannot carry a branch or pins.
150: 
151: Recommend A for assignment, with the facts roles need (branch, pins, fleet prefix) read from the existing sources in
152: their order: plugin options, store, herdr's file (the natural home of `fleet`). B is a later convenience.
153: 
154: ### e. MVP (2 to 4 pull requests)
155: 
156: | PR | Size | Content |
157: | -- | ---- | ------- |
158: | 1  | S    | Read-only gaps: block `env`/`printenv`/secret variables/credential paths for read-only agents (remove `env`, `printenv *` from `allow.json` or block in code), cases in `rules/cases.json`. No role needed; independent. |
159: | 2  | M-L  | `src/roles.ts` from the prototype (cwd tracking, write scope, git, gh, herdr, pins), `rules/roles.json` plus schema, `rules/cases-roles.json` run in the unit suite, CLI `check --role R --cwd D [--branch B] [--worktree W]` with the usual exit codes. No opencode behaviour change; `watch` becomes one call. |
160: | 3  | M    | Plugin: `roles` option (A); `tool.execute.before` blocks role violations (scope, push, merge, env, pins) for agents with a role; grants stay in the project's `opencode.json`; refuse to start a role whose user globs allow a write verb the guard cannot scope. |
161: | 4  | L    | Only if the maintainer chooses the catalogue: inject role globs with the strict rule (ask becomes block where a glob allows). Otherwise skip. |
162: 
163: Waits for 2.x: allow decided in code, pins without spelling-dependent globs, env prefixes, redirections on any stage,
164: roles applied without restart, answering prompts with the verdict.
165: 
166: ### f. Identity: does the role model change what the project is?
167: 
168: The data says what it protects is commands from unattended agents; "read-only" is the first and strictest role (and
169: stays the default). Three framings:
170: 
171: 1. "Read-only guard, and roles": keep the name and README opening; roles are an extension that begins with the CLI
172:    verdict (PR 2). Nothing renamed; the cost is a name that undersells the worker, orchestrator and deployer roles.
173: 2. "A role-based policy for unattended opencode agents": the plugin is a policy engine, read-only one profile. A rename
174:    would touch: package and repo name, CLI bin, plugin id, tool names `readonly_guard_*`, the review command and
175:    permission id, `READONLY_GUARD_*` variables, store, herdr and log file names and directories, error prefixes,
176:    docs and test fixtures, the maintainer's `file://` configs and any alias.
177: 3. "A verdict engine with front ends": the product is the engine (library plus CLI `check`/`role check`); the opencode
178:    plugin (1.x blocks, later 2.x hook) and a herdr coordinator integration are front ends. Biggest shift, and the
179:    most honest about the plugin only ever enforcing blocks on 1.x. Same rename categories as 2, plus a package split.
180: 
181: Rename is cheapest before the first npm publish, but none of PRs 1 to 3 needs it; framing 1 now and a decision at PR 4
182: or 2.x loses nothing.
183: 
184: ## 3. Not verified, and why
185: 
186: - opencode 2.x: no runtime here; `node_modules/@opencode-ai/plugin/dist/v2` has no permission hook type I could read
187:   (the sdk types mention permissions), so "the 2.x hook decides in code" is from TODO.md and README, not tested.
188: - A role-bearing agent run end to end through the real plugin: the prototype is unit-level plus hook facts; I did not
189:   build `dist/` or run the plugin with roles.
190: - Subagents of a worker (`task` to `general`) inheriting the role; `opencode --agent worker` started by the launcher;
191:   whether a herdr pane passes an env marker (option B); `external_directory` for `chown` and its ask-pattern shape.
192: - Symlink escapes and the time between hashing a pinned script and running it.
193: - Real models, real `gh` writes, any herdr control command: not run (cost, effect on the live session).
194: - Journal: the 163 notes are the coordinator's summaries, not raw commands, so command-level claims rest on the 36 raw
195:   ones; class borders are regex plus 18 hand overrides.
196: - Expected verdicts in `cases-roles.json` are my design intent; the maintainer has not ratified them.
197: 
198: ## 4. Recommendation
199: 
200: Design: roles are catalogue data plus one engine (`decideRole`) with three front ends: the CLI verdict, the 1.x
201: plugin hook (blocks only, strict rule), the 2.x permission hook (full decisions). Grants never come from user
202: patterns. Smallest useful slice: PR 1 (it fixes a real gap) and PR 2 (it replaces the coordinator's approval regexes
203: with the same engine the plugin will use, and the deploy pin becomes `sha256 + allowed arguments`). PR 3 then makes the
204: engine bite without granting anything. PR 4 and the catalogue of grants wait for decision 1 or for 2.x.
205: 
206: ## 5. Effort, risks and the test plan
207: 
208: - Sizes: S, M-L, M, L as in the table. Main risk: the parser approximates POSIX shell and the engine inherits its limits
209:   (eval, variables it cannot resolve are blocked, which over-blocks; the journal's interpreters stay asks).
210: - Risk of PR 4: a glob that allows plus code that fails to run is an unguarded write; the strict rule and "unknown agent
211:   means guarded" are mandatory (observed: `chat.params` always came first, but one miss would be fail-open).
212: - Risk: over-blocking an unattended worker stalls it; every block message must name the allowed alternative.
213: - Test plan: `rules/cases-roles.json` in the unit suite (every case through `decideRole`); a property test that the
214:   strict 1.x decider never allows what `decideRole` blocks or asks; schema tests for `roles.json`; an integration test
215:   driving a worker agent with the mock provider and checking the filesystem effects (the table in section c is the
216:   template, harness reusable from rog-redact); a leak test with fake secrets for the env and credential rules.
217: 
218: ## 6. Questions for the maintainer
219: 
220: 1. The invariant for write roles. (i) strict, narrow only: the plugin never grants; workers are enforced by blocks plus
221:    the project's allowlist (classify accepts 1 of 15 worker patterns, so grants live in `opencode.json`); safe by
222:    construction, but the fail-open ask-to-allow hole is still there for user-written globs unless the plugin refuses
223:    unscopable ones. (ii) catalogue: the package ships reviewed write capabilities (commit, own-branch push) that
224:    `classify.ts` alone refuses; works out of the box, but a bug in a catalogue rule is an allowed write, it needs
225:    the strict rule, and it makes the project a policy engine. (iii) decision service: the engine only answers
226:    verdicts, the coordinator stays the enforcement point (what happens today, minus the regexes); nothing to
227:    fail open, no value for a lone interactive user. (iv) do (iii) now and plug the engine into the 2.x hook later.
228:    I recommend (iii) then (iv), with the blocks of (i) in PR 3.
229: 2. For a role violation, `block` or `ask`? The corpus uses block for clear violations (push of another branch, merge,
230:    credentials) and ask for unverifiable ones; strict mode turns some asks into blocks.
231: 3. Take `env` and `printenv *` out of the shared allowlist now (PR 1)? It interacts with the redaction work.
232: 4. Is `HK=0` (skip hooks) a human decision always (the corpus says ask)? 7 journal lines show it approved by hand.
233: 5. Where do pins live and who signs them: the coordinator, in the store or a project-local file, never in the public repo?
234: 6. Role assignment: by agent name (A) or a launcher-written marker (B)?
235: 7. Is the reviewer role wanted, and should `gh` reads (`pr view/diff/checks`) join the shared read-only allowlist?
236: 8. Scratch: `.state/<agent>/tmp` inside the worktree (the corpus) or also a directory outside it?
237: 9. Name: decide at PR 2, PR 4 or 2.x?

(End of file - total 237 lines)
</content>

// `opencode run` against the mock: does it work in the harness, does the shell.env hook fire, does blanking apply?
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process"
import { assertNoLeaks, keepEvidence, lab } from "./lib.ts"

const l = await lab({
  name: "run",
  setup: ({ fakes }) => ({
    plugin: { shellEnv: { blank: Object.keys(fakes.env) }, hooks: { after: "observe" } },
    script: {
      scenarios: {
        "SCENARIO:runtest": [
          { tools: [{ name: "bash", args: { command: "printenv [redacted:envvar]; echo rc=$?", description: "print" } }] },
          { text: "done" },
        ],
      },
    },
  }),
})
try {
  const run = spawnSync("opencode", ["run", "-m", "mock/scripted", "SCENARIO:runtest"], {
    cwd: l.box.project,
    env: l.box.env,
    encoding: "utf8",
    timeout: 90_000,
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
  })
  const label = (text: string) => {
    let out = text
    for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(l.fakes.env)) out = out.split(value).join(`<${name}>`)
    return out
  }
  const trace = l.trace()
  const parts = l.parts().map((p) => JSON.parse(p.data)).filter((d) => d.type === "tool")
  const summary = {
    status: run.status,
    signal: run.signal,
    stdout: label(run.stdout ?? "").slice(0, 1500),
    stderr: label(run.stderr ?? "").slice(0, 1500),
    shellEnvCalls: trace.filter((t) => t.hook === "shell.env").length,
    afterCalls: trace.filter((t) => t.hook === "tool.execute.after").length,
    toolOutputs: parts.map((d) => label(String(d.state?.output ?? d.state?.error ?? ""))),
    requests: l.mock.requests().length,
  }
  console.log(JSON.stringify(summary, null, 1))
  keepEvidence(l, "04b-run", summary)
} finally {
  assertNoLeaks(l)
}

// R6: detection. Speed on 1 MB, recall per detector, false positives on an ordinary corpus, and the value-policy
// applied to environments. Only fake secrets are inserted; the real environment is only COUNTED (never printed).
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { alnum, evidenceDir, fakeSecrets } from "./lib.ts"
// @ts-expect-error plain JS module
import { collectSecretValues, createRedactor, SECRET_NAME, skipReason } from "./redactor.js"

const root = join(import.meta.dir, "../../..")
const walk = (dir: string, out: string[] = []): string[] => {
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const path = join(dir, name)
    const info = statSync(path)
    if (info.isDirectory()) walk(path, out)
    else if (/\.(ts|md|json|lock|js)$/.test(name) || name === "bun.lock") out.push(path)
  }
  return out
}
// an ordinary corpus: this repository's sources, rules, tests, lockfile and the plugin type definitions
const sources = [
  ...walk(join(root, "src")),
  ...walk(join(root, "rules")),
  ...walk(join(root, "test")),
  join(root, "README.md"),
  join(root, "bun.lock"),
  ...walk(join(root, "node_modules/@opencode-ai/plugin/dist")),
  ...walk(join(root, "node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist")).slice(0, 60),
]
let clean = ""
for (const path of sources) {
  clean += readFileSync(path, "utf8")
  if (clean.length >= 1_000_000) break
}
clean = clean.slice(0, 1_000_000)

const fakes = fakeSecrets()
const values = Object.entries(fakes.env).map(([name, value]) => ({ name, value }))
// secrets of the kinds a session meets, as (label, text, which detectors should catch it)
const inserted: { label: string; text: string }[] = [
  ...values.map(({ name, value }) => ({ label: `env-value ${name}`, text: `result: ${value} end` })),
  { label: "aws-akia (shape)", text: `aws_access_key_id AKIA${alnum(16).toUpperCase()}` },
  { label: "github_pat (shape)", text: `token github_pat_${alnum(40)}` },
  { label: "gho oauth (shape)", text: `oauth_token: gho_${alnum(36)}` },
  { label: "slack (shape)", text: `xoxb-${alnum(12)}-${alnum(12)}` },
  { label: "sk- key (shape)", text: `OPENAI sk-${alnum(40)}` },
  { label: "jwt (shape)", text: `eyJ${alnum(20)}.eyJ${alnum(30)}.${alnum(20)}` },
  { label: "bearer header (shape)", text: `Authorization: Bearer ${alnum(30)}` },
  { label: "private key block (shape)", text: `[redacted:secret]` },
  { label: "url credentials (shape)", text: `postgres://app:${alnum(16)}@db.internal/prod` },
  { label: "other-host [redacted:envvar]= (context)", text: `[redacted:envvar]=${alnum(14)}` },
  { label: "other-host json secret (context)", text: `"client_secret": "${alnum(24)}"` },
  { label: "hosts.yml oauth_token (context)", text: `    oauth_token: ${alnum(30)}` },
  { label: "bare unknown 40-char (none)", text: `value ${alnum(40)} end` },
]
const insertions = inserted.map((entry, i) => ({ ...entry, at: Math.floor(((i + 1) * clean.length) / (inserted.length + 1)) }))
let dirty = ""
let last = 0
for (const entry of [...insertions].sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at)) {
  // insert on a line of its own
  const cut = clean.indexOf("\n", entry.at)
  dirty += `${clean.slice(last, cut + 1)}${entry.text}\n`
  last = cut + 1
}
dirty += clean.slice(last)
// the secret part of each inserted text: what must not survive
const secretPart = (entry: { label: string; text: string }) => {
  const m = /(ghp_|npm_|sk_live_|sk-|gho_|github_pat_|xoxb-|AKIA|eyJ|hunter2-)[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/.exec(entry.text)
  if (m) return m[0]
  const long = /[A-Za-z0-9]{14,}/.exec(entry.text.replace(/^[^=:]*[=:]\s*"?/, ""))
  return long?.[0] ?? entry.text
}

const median = (xs: number[]) => [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b)[Math.floor(xs.length / 2)]!
const time = (fn: () => void, runs = 7) => {
  fn()
  const ms: number[] = []
  for (let i = 0; i < runs; i++) {
    const t = performance.now()
    fn()
    ms.push(performance.now() - t)
  }
  return Math.round(median(ms) * 10) / 10
}

const configs: [string, Record<string, unknown>][] = [
  ["values split (8 values)", { shapes: false, context: false }],
  ["values regex-alternation (8)", { shapes: false, context: false, strategy: "regex" }],
  ["shapes naive", { values: [], shapes: true, context: false, fast: false }],
  ["shapes + literal prefilter", { values: [], shapes: true, context: false, fast: true }],
  ["context naive", { values: [], shapes: false, context: true, fast: false }],
  ["context + word prefilter", { values: [], shapes: false, context: true, fast: true }],
  ["ALL naive", { shapes: true, context: true, fast: false }],
  ["ALL fast", { shapes: true, context: true, fast: true }],
]
const timing: Record<string, unknown>[] = []
const recall: Record<string, Record<string, string>> = {}
for (const [name, opts] of configs) {
  const r = createRedactor({ values, ...opts })
  const cleanMs = time(() => r.redact(clean))
  const dirtyMs = time(() => r.redact(dirty))
  const out = r.redact(dirty)
  timing.push({ detector: name, cleanMs, dirtyMs })
  for (const entry of insertions) {
    ;(recall[entry.label] ??= {})[name] = out.includes(secretPart(entry)) ? "LEAK" : "ok"
  }
}
console.table(timing)

// recall of the three detectors alone and combined (fast variants)
const detectors: [string, Record<string, unknown>][] = [
  ["values", { shapes: false, context: false }],
  ["shapes", { values: [], shapes: true, context: false }],
  ["context", { values: [], shapes: false, context: true }],
  ["all", { shapes: true, context: true }],
]
const matrix: Record<string, Record<string, string>> = {}
for (const [name, opts] of detectors) {
  const r = createRedactor({ values, ...opts })
  const out = r.redact(dirty)
  for (const entry of insertions) (matrix[entry.label] ??= {})[name] = out.includes(secretPart(entry)) ? "LEAK" : "ok"
}
console.table(matrix)

// false positives on the ordinary corpus
const kinds: Record<string, number> = {}
const fpRedactor = createRedactor({
  values,
  format: (kind: string) => {
    kinds[kind] = (kinds[kind] ?? 0) + 1
    return `[redacted:${kind}]`
  },
})
fpRedactor.redact(clean)
console.log("replacements on the ordinary corpus (1 MB, no secret inserted):", JSON.stringify(kinds))

// the value policy on environments: only counts for the real one
const realEnv = collectSecretValues(process.env as Record<string, string>)
const realNames = Object.keys(process.env).filter((n) => SECRET_NAME.test(n)).length
const trickyEnv: Record<string, string> = {
  SSH_AUTH_SOCK: "/run/user/1000/keyring/ssh",
  GPG_AGENT_INFO: "/run/user/1000/gnupg/S.gpg-agent:0:1",
  [redacted:envvar]: "1234567890123456",
  [redacted:envvar]: "1:Abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ABCD",
  AUTH_MODE: "oauth",
  TOKEN_TTL: "3600",
  PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH: "12",
  COOKIE_SECURE: "true",
  PASSWORD_PROMPT: "changeme",
  API_KEY_FILE: "/etc/keys/api.key",
  GIT_ASKPASS: "/usr/lib/git-core/git-gui--askpass",
  KEYRING_BACKEND: "gnome-keyring",
  SECRET_STORE_URL: "https://vault.internal:8200",
  [redacted:envvar]: "p@ss",
}
const tricky = collectSecretValues(trickyEnv)
const summary = {
  corpusBytes: clean.length,
  dirtyBytes: dirty.length,
  inserted: insertions.length,
  timing,
  recall,
  matrix,
  falsePositivesOnCleanCorpus: kinds,
  realEnvironment: {
    variablesWithSecretLookingNames: realNames,
    collectedAfterPolicy: realEnv.found.length,
    skipped: realEnv.skipped,
    minValueLength: realEnv.found.length ? Math.min(...realEnv.found.map((f: { value: string }) => f.value.length)) : null,
  },
  trickyEnvironment: {
    collected: tricky.found.map((f: { name: string }) => f.name),
    skipped: tricky.skipped,
    reasons: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(trickyEnv).map(([k, v]) => [k, skipReason(v) ?? "kept"])),
  },
}
writeFileSync(join(evidenceDir, "06-detection.json"), `${JSON.stringify(summary, null, 1)}\n`)
console.log(JSON.stringify({ realEnvironment: summary.realEnvironment, trickyEnvironment: summary.trickyEnvironment }, null, 1))
---

1121 18:05:51
// An ordinary 1 MB corpus (no secret in it): this repository's sources, rules, tests, lockfile and plugin typings.
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"

const root = join(import.meta.dir, "../../..")
const walk = (dir: string, out: string[] = []): string[] => {
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const path = join(dir, name)
    const info = statSync(path)
    if (info.isDirectory()) walk(path, out)
    else if (/\.(ts|md|json|lock|js)$/.test(name) || name === "bun.lock") out.push(path)
  }
  return out
}

export function ordinaryCorpus(bytes = 1_000_000): string {
  const sources = [
    ...walk(join(root, "src")),
    ...walk(join(root, "rules")),
    ...walk(join(root, "test")),
    join(root, "README.md"),
    join(root, "bun.lock"),
    ...walk(join(root, "node_modules/@opencode-ai/plugin/dist")),
    ...walk(join(root, "node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist")).slice(0, 60),
  ]
  let text = ""
  for (const path of sources) {
    text += readFileSync(path, "utf8")
    if (text.length >= bytes) break
  }
  return text.slice(0, bytes)
}

```

import { parseArgs } from "node:util"

const { values } = parseArgs({
  options: {
    to: { type: "string" }, // full package name: opencode-<short>
    command: { type: "string" }, // review command, default <short>-review
    "from-dir": { type: "string" },
    into: { type: "string" },
  },
})
const pkg = values.to
if (!pkg || !values["from-dir"] || !values.into) throw new Error("usage: --to <pkg> --from-dir <checkout> --into <dir>")
const short = pkg.replace(/^opencode-/, "")
const command = values.command ?? `${short}-review`
const snake = short.replaceAll("-", "_")
const upper = snake.toUpperCase()

// [pattern, replacement], in this order
const families: [RegExp, string][] = [
  [/opencode-readonly-guard/g, pkg], // package, bin, plugin id, repo URL, schema $id, CLI name
  [/READONLY_GUARD/g, upper], // env vars
  [/readonly_guard/g, snake], // tool ids and the confirmation permission
  [/guard-review/g, command], // the review command
  [/readonly-guard/g, short], // store file, log dir, herdr file, error prefixes, prose
]

mkdirSync(values.into, { recursive: true })
const tar = execFileSync("git", ["archive", "HEAD"], { cwd: values["from-dir"], maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 })
execFileSync("tar", ["-x", "-C", values.into], { input: tar })

const binary = /\.(png|jpg|ico|gz|zip|lock)$/
function walk(dir: string, rel = ""): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir).flatMap((name) => {
    const path = join(dir, name)
    const r = rel ? `${rel}/${name}` : name
    return statSync(path).isDirectory() ? walk(path, r) : [r]
  })
}

let changed = 0
for (const rel of walk(values.into)) {
  if (rel.startsWith("memory/") || binary.test(rel)) continue
  const path = join(values.into, rel)
  const before = readFileSync(path, "utf8")
  // The copies registry keys (src/copies.ts, pinned by test/unit/copies.test.ts) are how an old build and a renamed
  // build still loaded side by side find each other: keep them (scenario B in evidence/sidebyside.txt).
  let after = before.replace(/opencode-readonly-guard(\.(?:copies|failed)\.v1)/g, "\u0000KEEP$1")
  for (const [re, to] of families) after = after.replace(re, to)
  after = after.replace(/\u0000KEEP/g, "opencode-readonly-guard")
  if (after !== before) {
    writeFileSync(path, after)
    changed++
  }
}
// bun.lock is text: its workspace name is the package name
const lock = join(values.into, "bun.lock")
writeFileSync(lock, readFileSync(lock, "utf8").replaceAll("opencode-readonly-guard", pkg))
console.log(`renamed to ${pkg} (short ${short}, command ${command}, env ${upper}_*): ${changed} files rewritten`)

```

# What does `rtk env` do with an environment dump? A CLEARED environment: only the fakes below exist (the real
# environment never enters a pipe). Fakes are generated here, not typed.
tok() { head -c 400 /dev/urandom | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c "$1"; }
FAKE_GH="ghp_$(tok 36)"
FAKE_AWS="$(tok 40)"
FAKE_PW="hunter2-$(tok 10)"
out=$(env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=/nonexistent [redacted:envvar]="$FAKE_GH" [redacted:envvar]="$FAKE_AWS" [redacted:envvar]="$FAKE_PW" FAKE_PLAIN=value123 rtk env 2>&1)
echo "--- rtk env (cleared environment, fakes only):"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -e "s/$FAKE_GH/<FAKE-GH-VALUE>/g" -e "s/$FAKE_AWS/<FAKE-AWS-VALUE>/g" -e "s/$FAKE_PW/<FAKE-PW-VALUE>/g" | head -30
for v in "$FAKE_GH" "$FAKE_AWS" "$FAKE_PW"; do
  if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$v"; then echo "value present in rtk env output: yes"; else echo "value present in rtk env output: no"; fi
done
echo "--- rtk env -f TOKEN (filter):"
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=/nonexistent [redacted:envvar]="$FAKE_GH" rtk env -f TOKEN 2>&1 | sed -e "s/$FAKE_GH/<FAKE-GH-VALUE>/g" | head -10

```

// R5: the plugin's own event log (src/log.ts). A shell command that holds a (fake) secret is logged as typed: the
// `call`, `blocked` and `asked` events carry it. Redacting at write time is one wrapper around `write`.
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { createLog } from "../../../src/log.ts"
import { alnum, scratch } from "./lib.ts"
// @ts-expect-error plain JS module
import { createRedactor } from "./redactor.js"

const token = `ghp_${alnum(36)}`
const dir = join(scratch, "eventlog")
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
const plain = createLog(join(dir, "plain"))
const redactor = createRedactor({ values: [{ name: "[redacted:envvar]", value: token }] })
const inner = createLog(join(dir, "redacted"))
const redacting = {
  ...inner,
  write(event: Parameters<typeof inner.write>[0]) {
    redactor.redactDeep(event, { event }, "event")
    inner.write(event)
  },
}
for (const log of [plain, redacting]) {
  log.write({ type: "call", agent: "plan", command: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${token}" https://example.invalid/` })
  log.write({ type: "asked", agent: "plan", patterns: [`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${token}" *`], command: `curl -u me:${token} x` })
}
const count = (file: string) => readFileSync(file, "utf8").split(token).length - 1
console.log(JSON.stringify({ plainLogHits: count(plain.file), redactedLogHits: count(inner.file) }))
---

// What a redactor that matches values and shapes cannot see: the same secret after a transformation the model
// (or a command) applies. In-process, fake secret.
import { alnum } from "./lib.ts"
// @ts-expect-error plain JS module
import { createRedactor } from "./redactor.js"

const token = `ghp_${alnum(36)}`
const r = createRedactor({ values: [{ name: "[redacted:envvar]", value: token }] })
const hex = (s: string) => Buffer.from(s).toString("hex")
const cases: Record<string, string> = {
  "plain": token,
  "base64": Buffer.from(token).toString("base64"),
  "base64url": Buffer.from(token).toString("base64url"),
  "hex": hex(token),
  "reversed": [...token].reverse().join(""),
  "url-encoded (no change)": encodeURIComponent(token),
  "JSON-escaped": JSON.stringify(token).slice(1, -1),
  "split in two lines (fold -w 20)": `${token.slice(0, 20)}\n${token.slice(20)}`,
  "chars spaced (sed 's/./& /g')": [...token].join(" "),
  "first 12 chars only (${T:0:12})": token.slice(0, 12),
  "first 30 chars": token.slice(0, 30),
  "last 20 chars": token.slice(-20),
  "rot13": token.replace(/[a-z]/gi, (c) => String.fromCharCode(c.charCodeAt(0) + (c.toLowerCase() < "n" ? 13 : -13))),
  "sha256 (not a secret anymore)": new Bun.CryptoHasher("sha256").update(token).digest("hex"),
}
const result: Record<string, string> = {}
for (const [name, text] of Object.entries(cases)) {
  const out = r.redact(`value: ${text} end`)
  // does the output still let the model reconstruct the token? crude: contains >= 12 chars of it, or an encoding of it
  const survivors = out.includes(text)
  result[name] = survivors ? "SURVIVES" : "redacted"
}
console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 1))
