Fail-open risk: a glob\n  allows, the code fails to run, a write goes through. The strict rule (an ask becomes a block where a glob allows) removes the 4 unsafe allows measured on the corpus.\n- Role assignment options (decided in T-014): by agent name in the plugin options or the store (recommended, extends `agents`), or by a launcher-written marker.\n- `chat.params` always preceded `tool.execute.before` of its session in 20 of 20 observed calls; an agent whose role is unknown must still be guarded (unknown means guarded).\n\n## Binding decisions\n- Option shape (example, to be confirmed in the plan): `{\"roles\": {\"plan\": \"read-only\", \"worker\": {\"role\": \"worker\", \"scripts\": [{\"path\": \"...\", \"sha256\": \"...\"}]}}}`; `agents.include/exclude`\n  remain as sugar. A role names catalogue items and never brings patterns; user patterns still go through `classifyPattern`.\n- Refuse to start a role whose user globs allow a write verb the guard cannot scope (message names the glob).\n- Every new hook path checks `copy.active()`.\n- Integration tests with the mock provider (T-010) for: a worker role blocked from pushing another branch, a read-only role unchanged, an unknown agent guarded.\n\n## Plan\nSTAGE 0 PLAN (max 15 lines) and go; test-first; `mise run check`; `mise run test:integration`; PR.\n\n## Definition of Done\nRole violations of the corpus that are blockable on 1.x are blocked in a real opencode run; the ones that need 2.x are listed in the README (\"What it does not do\"); PR open.\n\n## Out of scope\nGrants, the 2.x hook (M-004).\n\n## Changelog\n- 2026-11-16: created (WP7).\n"

Copy it ONCE.\n2. In the GitHub repository: Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions, new repository secret `[redacted:envvar]`. Paste, save. Do not keep the token anywhere else; never paste it into a\n   conversation with an agent.\n3. After the release PR (T-009) is merged, push the tag yourself: `git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0`. The `release.yml` workflow (permissions `id-token: write`, Node 24, `npm publish`)\n   publishes and generates the provenance attestation (needs a public repository and `repository.url` in `package.json` equal to the GitHub repository).\n4. Check: `npm view opencode-agent-policy`, the provenance badge on the package page, `npx oap --version`.\n   (`npx` runs the sole `bin` of a package: not tested yet).\n\n## Then, before the SECOND release: switch to trusted publishing, drop the token\n1. Configure the trusted publisher of the package, either on npmjs.com (package Settings, Trusted Publisher, GitHub Actions: user `silopolis`, repository `opencode-agent-policy`,\n   workflow file `release.yml`, no environment) or with `npm trust github opencode-agent-policy --file release.yml --repo [redacted:repo] --allow-publish`\n   (needs the account 2FA; it asks for a one-time code; the website offers a 5-minute window without repeated codes).\n2.   "content": "# Lessons from running unattended agents under the guard (input of T-002)\n\nSource: the coordinator's notes of one week of work (about a dozen build workers, three research workers, deploy sessions, the maintainer in the loop). Public-safe: no host, user or private\nrepository names. Each lesson says what happened or what was measured.\n\n## Secrets\n- **The incident class.** A worker ran `env | grep -E '^(GIT|HK)'`: the pattern also matched `[redacted:envvar]`; the output entered the session, which is stored in the database and re-sent to the\n  provider on every turn. Rule since: never print the environment; check one variable with `[ -n \"${NAME:-}\" ]`; list names only with `env | cut -d= -f1 | sort`; experiments use fake secrets.\n- **Three more ways to print the environment without any prompt** were found later: `export -p` / `declare -p` (declarations are not command nodes, opencode never prompts for them), `ps e`, and reading\n  `/proc/*/environ`. The first two are blocked in code; the allowlist had `env` and `printenv *` on it (decision: ask, T-004).\n- **Revoking a leaked token is easy, getting the old value out of running processes is not.** Deleting the line that sets a variable in a shell profile does not unset it in processes that already\n  inherited it: a terminal multiplexer server and every pane it starts keep the old value; the GitHub CLI prefers the variable over its stored login, so after the revocation `gh`, the git credential\n  helper and any tool that calls `gh auth token` fail in those processes (401). The fix is an explicit `unset` in the profile and starting agents with an environment that does not hold secrets.\n- **Never run a command that could print a credential, even with redirects.** In zsh `cmd 2>&1 >/dev/null | next` still sends stdout into the pipe (multios). Compare secrets by hash, with\n  `2>/dev/null |`, and never to the terminal.\n- **Test harnesses leak too.** A sandbox helper that copies the caller's environment hands every credential to the child processes of the tests (all secret-named variables, a token among them).\n  Allowlist the environment, add fake secrets, and self-check the sandbox's files against the caller's real values.\n- Redaction is a safety net, not a boundary: transformed secrets (base64, split, reversed) defeat it; starting agents without secrets is the boundary.\n\n## Permission prompts\n- Answer \"Allow once\" only. Verify on the screen which option is highlighted before pressing Enter (a blind Enter once opened the \"Always allow\" confirmation).\n- Read every script a worker asks to run BEFORE answering, and read it again if it changed: a script was modified between the check and the answer once. Check in one step, answer in the next.\n- A long command is truncated by the dialog, even fullscreen; the end can hide a second command. Check the state before acting.\n\n## Orchestration\n- **Plan first, go second.** Every worker replies with a plan (max 15 to 20 lines) and waits. ```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# export-sessions.sh <worktree> <slug>=<session id>...
# Export OpenCode sessions with the fleet exporter (no --sanitize: it replaces the whole content with placeholders),
# redact each file with the fleet redactor in the public profile, verify with --check, delete the raw copies.
# Raw exports live only in a 0700 directory under .state/rog-orch/tmp/ and are removed at the end.
# Prints counts only; never prints transcript content.
set -uo pipefail
STATE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
WT=${1:?usage: export-sessions.sh <worktree> slug=session_id ...}; shift
RAW=$STATE/tmp/export-raw
REDACT=$HOME/.config/nvim/scripts/session_redact.py
EXPORTER=$HOME/Work/istc/scripts/session/export.py
PY=$HOME/Work/istc/.venv/bin/python
for v in $(env | cut -d= -f1 | grep -E '^GIT_'); do unset "$v"; done
rm -rf "$RAW" && install -d -m 0700 "$RAW"
trap 'rm -rf "$RAW"' EXIT
# After the fleet redactor: NUL bytes (raw strings from binaries make a file "binary" for git and GitHub) and the extra
# local terms of private/extra-terms.txt. Terms never enter the repository.
scrub() {
  python3 - "$1" "$STATE/private/extra-terms.txt" <<'PY'
import re, sys
path, terms_file = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
data = open(path, "rb").read().replace(b"\x00", b"\xe2\x90\x80")  # U+2400 SYMBOL FOR NULL
try:
    terms = [l.strip() for l in open(terms_file, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
except FileNotFoundError:
    terms = []
for term in terms:
    data = re.sub(re.escape(term.encode()), b"[redacted:private]", data, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
open(path, "wb").write(data)
PY
}
rc=0
for spec in "$@"; do
  slug=${spec%%=*} sid=${spec#*=}
  : >"$RAW/.before"; before=$(ls "$RAW" | sort)
  if ! (cd "$HOME/Work/istc" && timeout 900 "$PY" "$EXPORTER" "$sid" --slug "$slug" --out-dir "$RAW" >"$RAW/.log" 2>&1); then
    echo "FAIL export $slug"; tail -3 "$RAW/.log" | sed -E "s#$HOME#~#g"; rc=1; continue
  fi
  after=$(ls "$RAW" | sort); new=$(comm -13 <(echo "$before") <(echo "$after") | grep -v '^\.' || true)
  for f in $new; do
    ( cd "$WT" && "$PY" "$REDACT" --profile public <"$RAW/$f" >"memory/sessions/$f" ) || { echo "FAIL redact $f"; rc=1; continue; }
    scrub "$WT/memory/sessions/$f"
    printf '%-62s raw %8d B -> redacted %8d B\n' "$f" "$(wc -c <"$RAW/$f")" "$(wc -c <"$WT/memory/sessions/$f")"
  done
done
( cd "$WT" && "$PY" "$REDACT" --check >"$STATE/tmp/check.txt" 2>&1; echo "redactor --check exit $?"; grep -E ': [1-9]' "$STATE/tmp/check.txt" || echo "all categories 0" )
exit $rc
---

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# export-sessions.sh [--plan] <worktree> <slug>=<session id>...\n# Export OpenCode sessions with the fleet exporter (no --sanitize: it replaces the whole content with placeholders),\n# redact each file with the fleet redactor in the public profile, scrub locally, verify with --check, delete the raw copies.\n# Raw exports live only in a 0700 directory under .state/rog-orch/tmp/ and are removed at the end.\n# Prints counts only; never prints transcript content.\n#\n# RULE (maintainer, 2026-11-16): an export NEVER overwrites a previous export, above all for a long-running session continued\n# after a compaction. The exporter itself refuses to overwrite without --force; this wrapper never uses --force and never writes\n# over an existing file either:\n#   - a session already exported in <worktree>/memory/sessions (found by the \"**Session ID:**\" line of the file headers) is exported\n#     INCREMENTALLY: --since <marker of its latest part>, and the increment becomes a NEW file <stem>-pNN.md (the first file is part 1,\n#     so the first increment is p02). The increment re-emits the message of the marker (the exporter's \"inclusive\" bound).\n#   - nothing new since the marker: nothing is written.\n#   - a new session (or a child session) is written under the exporter's own name. If that name exists already: identical after\n#     redaction = skipped; different = FAILURE (a child that grew must be exported as a part by hand), never an overwrite.\n# --plan only prints, per session, the parts found, the marker, the newest message and what would be done.\nset -uo pipefail\nSTATE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\nplan=0; [ \"${1:-}\" = \"--plan\" ] && { plan=1; shift; }\nWT=${1:?usage: export-sessions.sh [--plan] <worktree> slug=session_id ...}; shift\nSESS=$WT/memory/sessions\nRAW=$STATE/tmp/export-raw\nREDACT=$HOME/.config/nvim/scripts/session_redact.py\nEXPORTER=$HOME/Work/istc/scripts/session/export.py\nPY=$HOME/Work/istc/.venv/bin/python\nDB=$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db\nfor v in $(env | cut -d= -f1 | grep -E '^GIT_'); do unset \"$v\"; done\n[ -d \"$SESS\" ] || { echo \"no $SESS\"; exit 64; }\nrm -rf \"$RAW\" && install -d -m 0700 \"$RAW\"\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$RAW\"' EXIT\n\n# After the fleet redactor: NUL bytes (raw strings from binaries make a file \"binary\" for git and GitHub), EXCISION of the output of\n# tool calls whose input matches private/excise-inputs.txt (content of private repositories: the redactor hides names, never content),\n# and the extra local terms of private/extra-terms.txt. Local files, never committed.\nscrub() {\n  python3 - \"$1\" \"$STATE/private/extra-terms.txt\" \"$STATE/private/excise-inputs.txt\" <<'PY'\nimport re, sys\npath, terms_file, excise_file = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]\ndata = open(path, \"rb\").read().replace(b\"\\x00\", b\"\\xe2\\x90\\x80\")  # U+2400 SYMBOL FOR NULL\n\ndef lines_of(f):\n    try:\n        return [l.strip() for l in open(f, encoding=\"utf-8\") if l.strip() and not l.startswith(\"#\")]\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return []\n\n# 1. EXCISE: the exporter fences outputs with plain triple backticks and an output body may hold inner fences and \"## \" lines, so an\n#    output is bounded by the exporter's own markers: the next \"**Tool: \" line or a \"## Assistant\" / \"## User\" heading; its closing\n#    fence is the last fence line before that.\npatterns = [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in lines_of(excise_file)]\ntext = data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"surrogateescape\")\nif patterns:\n    lines = text.split(\"\\n\")\n    out, i, n, cut = [], 0, len(lines), 0\n    boundary = re.compile(r\"^(\\*\\*Tool: |## (Assistant|User)\\b)\")\n    tool_start = None\n    while i < n:\n        line = lines[i]\n        if line.startswith(\"**Tool: \"):\n            tool_start = len(out)\n        if line == \"**Output:**\" and tool_start is not None and i + 1 < n and lines[i + 1] == \"```\":\n            block_input = \"\\n\".join(out[tool_start:])\n            if any(p.search(block_input) for p in patterns):\n                j = i + 2\n                while j < n and not boundary.match(lines[j]):\n                    j += 1\n                close = j - 1\n                while close > i + 1 and lines[close] != \"```\":\n                    close -= 1\n                if close > i + 1:\n                    out += [line, \"```\", \"[redacted:private: output of a command that read a private repository]\", \"```\"]\n                    i = close + 1\n                    cut += 1\n                    continue\n        out.append(line)\n        i += 1\n    text = \"\\n\".join(out)\n    sys.stderr.write(\"  excised outputs: %d\\n\" % cut)\ndata = text.encode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"surrogateescape\")\n\n# 2. extra private terms (substring, case-insensitive)\nfor term in lines_of(terms_file):\n    data = re.sub(re.escape(term.encode()), b\"[redacted:private]\", data, flags=re.IGNORECASE)\nopen(path, \"wb\").write(data)\nPY\n}\n\nHDR=24   # lines of a file header searched for the session id and the marker\npart_no() { local b; b=$(basename \"$1\" .md); if [[ $b =~ -p([0-9]+)$ ]]; then echo $((10#${BASH_REMATCH[1]})); else echo 1; fi; }\nheader_sid() { head -n \"$HDR\" \"$1\" | grep -a -m1 '^\\*\\*Session ID:\\*\\* ' | sed 's/^\\*\\*Session ID:\\*\\* //; s/[[:space:]]*$//'; }\nmarker_of() { head -n \"$HDR\" \"$1\" | grep -ao -m1 'session-export: through msg_[A-Za-z0-9]*' | sed 's/.*through //'; }\nstem_of() { local b; b=$(basename \"$1\" .md); echo \"${b%-p[0-9][0-9]}\"; }\n\nshapes='gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{40,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|npm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}'\nrc=0\nfor spec in \"$@\"; do\n  slug=${spec%%=*} sid=${spec#*=}\n  [[ $sid =~ ^ses_[A-Za-z0-9]+$ ]] || { echo \"FAIL bad session id for $slug\"; rc=1; continue; }\n  echo \"== $slug\"\n  # 1. what is already exported for this session: the latest part and its marker\n  last=\"\" lastn=0 nparts=0\n  for f in \"$SESS\"/*.md; do\n    [ -e \"$f\" ] || continue\n    [ \"$(basename \"$f\")\" = README.md ] && continue\n    [ \"$(header_sid \"$f\")\" = \"$sid\" ] || continue\n    nparts=$((nparts + 1)); n=$(part_no \"$f\")\n    if [ \"$n\" -gt \"$lastn\" ]; then lastn=$n; last=$f; fi\n  done\n  since=() ; marker=\"\"\n  if [ \"$nparts\" -gt 0 ]; then\n    marker=$(marker_of \"$last\")\n    [ -n \"$marker\" ] || { echo \"  FAIL: latest part $(basename \"$last\") has no session-export marker: cannot continue safely\"; rc=1; continue; }\n    newest=$(sqlite3 -readonly \"$DB\" \"select id from message where session_id='$sid' order by time_created desc, id desc limit 1\")\n    echo \"  parts found: $nparts (latest: $(basename \"$last\"), through ${marker:0:20}...), newest message in the database: ${newest:0:20}...\"\n    if [ \"$marker\" = \"$newest\" ]; then echo \"  up to date: nothing to export\"; continue; fi\n    since=(--since \"$marker\")\n    echo \"  -> increment, new file part $(printf '%02d' $((lastn + 1)))\"\n  else\n    echo \"  not exported yet: full export under the exporter's own name\"\n  fi\n  [ \"$plan\" = 1 ] && continue\n\n  # 2. export into a fresh directory (the exporter never overwrites without --force, and we never pass it)\n  out=$RAW/$slug; install -d -m 0700 \"$out\" \"$out/processed\"\n  if ! (cd \"$HOME/Work/istc\" && timeout 900 \"$PY\" \"$EXPORTER\" \"$sid\" --slug \"$slug\" \"${since[@]}\" --out-dir \"$out\" >\"$RAW/.log\" 2>&1); then\n    echo \"  FAIL export\"; tail -3 \"$RAW/.log\" | sed -E \"s#$HOME#~#g\"; rc=1; continue\n  fi\n  produced=$(cd \"$out\" && ls -1 ./*.md 2>/dev/null | sed 's#^\\./##' || true)\n  [ -n \"$produced\" ] || { echo \"  FAIL: the exporter produced no file\"; rc=1; continue; }\n  for f in $produced; do\n    fsid=$(header_sid \"$out/$f\")\n    if [ \"$fsid\" = \"$sid\" ] && [ \"$nparts\" -gt 0 ]; then\n      target=\"$(stem_of \"$out/$f\")-p$(printf '%02d' $((lastn + 1))).md\"\n    else\n      target=$f\n    fi\n    ( cd \"$WT\" && \"$PY\" \"$REDACT\" --profile public <\"$out/$f\" >\"$out/processed/$target\" ) || { echo \"  FAIL redact $f\"; rc=1; continue; }\n    scrub \"$out/processed/$target\"\n    dest=$SESS/$target\n    if [ -e \"$dest\" ]; then\n      if cmp -s \"$out/processed/$target\" \"$dest\"; then echo \"  unchanged, skipped: $target\"; continue; fi\n      echo \"  FAIL: $target exists and differs: NOT overwritten (a child session that grew must be exported as a part by hand)\"; rc=1; continue\n    fi\n    cp -n \"$out/processed/$target\" \"$dest\"\n    printf '  NEW %-66s raw %8d B -> redacted %8d B\\n' \"$target\" \"$(wc -c <\"$out/$f\")\" \"$(wc -c <\"$dest\")\"\n    # token SHAPES, counts only (never the values): the redactor must turn every one into a marker. A revoked value is in no process any more,\n    # so the shape count is the check.\n    printf '    token shapes: raw %s -> redacted %s (must be 0)\\n' \"$(grep -aoE \"$shapes\" \"$out/$f\" | wc -l)\" \"$(grep -aoE \"$shapes\" \"$dest\" | wc -l)\"\n  done\ndone\n[ \"$plan\" = 1 ] && exit \"$rc\"\n( cd \"$WT\" && \"$PY\" \"$REDACT\" --check >\"$STATE/tmp/check.txt\" 2>&1; echo \"redactor --check exit $?\"; grep -E ': [1-9]' \"$STATE/tmp/check.txt\" || echo \"all categories 0\" )\nexit \"$rc\"\n"
}
